sections.title: Volume Drivers
sections.subtitle: South Port's revenue is largely volume-linked. Cargo tonnage, Tiwai smelter volume and container throughput are the operating drivers behind every line in the financials below.

cargoVolume.title: Total Cargo Volume
cargoVolume.content:
Total physical weight of cargo handled across all trade types — bulk, container and Tiwai Wharf — measured in million tonnes. This is the single most important operating KPI: nearly all of South Port's wharfage, cargo-handling and marine revenue is volume-linked.

For South Port: tonnage grew from 2.72m tonnes (FY2014) to a record 3.96m tonnes (FY2026), a ~3.05% 10-year CAGR, but FY2026 was flattered by a one-off wind-farm turbine cargo intake and a wind-throw log surge. Management explicitly guides FY2027 volumes broadly flat versus FY2026.

What to watch:

  • Whether FY2027 volumes hold near the FY2026 level once one-off project cargo drops out
  • Any recurrence of the Tiwai demand-response curtailment that depressed FY2025
  • Conversion of the ~1,851MW regional wind-farm pipeline into further project cargo over the next 5-10 years

volumeMix.title: Bulk vs Container vs Tiwai Volume
volumeMix.content:
The three components of total cargo tonnage: bulk (fertiliser, stock feed, cement, forestry, alumina — 59% of FY26 volume), container (17%) and Tiwai Wharf cargo tied to the NZAS aluminium smelter (24%).

For South Port: Tiwai volume is the key concentration risk: it rose 16.1% in FY2026 to 942,000 tonnes as NZAS's third potline returned to full operation after the Feb-2025 Meridian Energy demand-response curtailment, but the same curtailment mechanism (up to 185MW under the 20-year NZAS power agreements) can recur in any dry, high-demand year. The disclosed breakdown only extends to the last two fiscal years in this dataset.

What to watch:

  • Tiwai volume stability as the clearest read on smelter operating rate
  • Bulk growth from agriculture/forestry versus Tiwai's more binary risk profile

teu.title: Container Volume (TEU)
teu.content:
Twenty-foot Equivalent Unit — the standard container-counting measure, distinct from bulk and Tiwai tonnage.

For South Port: FY2026's record 62,000 TEU (+18.5% YoY) was driven by two new shipping services: the MSC Eagle Service (direct US East Coast/Europe link via Panama, launched Feb-2026) and an enhanced Trans-Tasman Southern Loop, alongside rising MSC Wallaby Service frequency.

What to watch:

  • Whether the new services sustain call frequency into FY2027 or represent a one-off step-up
  • Dairy/meat export container volumes as a read on Southland agricultural output, especially with softer Fonterra farmgate milk price guidance

revenue.title: Revenue & YoY Growth
revenue.content:
Total operating revenue — wharfage, cargo handling, storage/warehousing, marine services and property/lease income — and its year-on-year growth rate.

For South Port: revenue grew from $31.3m (FY2014) to $71.8m (FY2026), a ~6.9% 10-year CAGR, roughly double the ~3.05% volume CAGR — reflecting price/mix gains on top of tonnage growth. FY2026's +13.5% is a record-year outlier, boosted by one-off wind-farm project cargo that management says will not repeat in FY2027.

What to watch:

  • Whether FY2027 growth reverts toward the historical ~4-7% range as guided
  • Price/mix versus pure volume as the driver of any further growth

ebitdaMargin.title: EBITDA Margin
ebitdaMargin.content:
EBITDA as a percentage of operating revenue — the key operating-leverage measure for a fixed-cost port business.

For South Port: margin has ranged 38.0%-43.5% over the past decade (10-year mean 41.1%), with FY2026 at 41.6%, above the disclosed NZ port-sector average (~38% FY25) but below SPN's own FY2022 peak of 43.5%. The DCF's base case holds margin at a mid-cycle 40.0-40.5%, not the FY2026 level, because FY2026 also carries one-off project cargo.

What to watch:

  • Whether margin holds above 40% as project-cargo tailwinds fade in FY2027
  • Any capex-driven cost step-up from the pending Port Planning Exercise (results due late Sept 2026)

npat.title: Reported vs Normalised NPAT
npat.content:
Reported statutory net profit after tax against management's normalised NPAT, which strips out one-off tax and non-operating items.

For South Port: FY2024 reported NPAT of $7.376m was distorted by a one-off $2.3m deferred-tax expense from the March-2024 removal of tax depreciation on commercial buildings; normalised NPAT that year was $9.956m. FY2026 reported and normalised NPAT are close ($16.11m vs $16.14m), so the FY2024 gap is the exception, not the rule.

What to watch:

  • Any further one-off tax or valuation items that widen the reported/normalised gap
  • Normalised NPAT as management's own preferred earnings measure for guidance and dividend-cover discussions

fcf.title: Operating Cash Flow, CapEx & Free Cash Flow
fcf.content:
Operating cash flow less capital expenditure — the cash actually available for dividends, debt paydown and growth investment.

For South Port: FCF is structurally lumpy because capex is lumpy: $2.5m in FY2017 versus a $24.4m channel-deepening peak in FY2022 (FCF went negative that year). FY2026's $14.2m owner FCF is roughly 2.2x the 8-year raw-dollar median, largely because FY2022-24 was a capex supercycle; on a normalised-capex-margin basis FY2026 is only ~1.12x the median. The DCF does not carry FY2026 forward — it rebuilds Year-1 owner FCF mid-cycle at $12.9m using a 13% capex ratio (the 10-year median) rather than management's own lower maintenance-only 'operating free cash flow' figure.

What to watch:

  • The scale and timing of the next capex cycle: a replacement tug and mobile harbour crane are flagged short-to-medium term, plus potential findings from the 30-year Port Planning Exercise (due late Sept 2026)
  • Whether capex reverts toward the 13% of revenue mid-cycle average or spikes again as in FY2021-22

netDebt.title: Total Debt vs Cash
netDebt.content:
Gross borrowings against cash on hand. Lease liabilities are immaterial here ($0.205m) and are not part of this comparison.

For South Port: gross debt was flat at $31.0m FY2025-FY2026, but net debt fell to $18.5m (from $25m) as cash built to $12.6m, taking Debt/EBITDA to 0.6x (from 1.0x) with $19m of covenant headroom against a long-term gearing target of <2.0x. This is currently a low-risk balance sheet, though a future capex cycle (as in FY2021-24) would re-lever the company.

What to watch:

  • Whether the pending Port Planning Exercise capex findings require fresh borrowing
  • Gearing trajectory relative to the <2.0x Net Debt/EBITDA target

dividend.title: Dividend per Share
dividend.content:
Total dividends declared per ordinary share for the fiscal year, fully imputed. South Port is majority council-owned (~66% Environment Southland) with a small, illiquid free float and is best understood as an income holding rather than a growth compounder.

For South Port: DPS has risen every year in this 10-year window with no cut, including through the FY2024 tax-distorted trough: 23.0c (FY2015) → 26.0c (FY2017-21) → 27.0c (FY2022-24) → 28.0c (FY2025) → 29.0c (FY2026). FY2026's payout ratio was 47% of NPAT, covered ~1.8x by owner FCF ($14.0m owner FCF vs ~$7.6m paid). At the $8.92 price this is a 4.5% gross imputed yield.

What to watch:

  • Dividend cover if a Tiwai curtailment repeat or a large capex cycle pressures owner FCF
  • No explicit FY2027 cents-per-share target has been given; management reiterated only a qualitative commitment to "sustainable shareholder returns"
